name: structured_resources
description: Curated catalog of dynamic-network rules for the viva-dynamic-networks investigation. Two families: (A) network-rule — dynamics OF the network, topology-reconfiguring rules implemented as process-bigraph reactions; and (B) network-dynamics — dynamics ON the network, state evolving on nodes/edges (the later SBML-at-nodes + inter-node transport studies). Each card cross-links to the primary / review references folded into the References list below.

network-rule.name: Erdős–Rényi random growth
network-rule.summary: Baseline null model. Edges appear (or vanish) uniformly at random, independent of node identity or degree — no structure beyond chance.
network-rule.rule: At each step add/remove an edge between a uniformly random pair of nodes with probability p (or add n nodes and wire each pair independently w.p. p).
network-rule.emergent: Poisson/binomial degree distribution; sharp giant-component percolation at <k>=1.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'random_edge' picks two random node schema keys and sets an edge entry.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 1 null baseline — the no-rule control every other rule is read against.

network-rule.name: Barabási–Albert preferential attachment
network-rule.summary: "Rich get richer" growth: arriving nodes link to existing nodes with probability proportional to current degree, producing scale-free hubs.
network-rule.rule: Each step a new node arrives with m edges; it attaches to existing node i with probability Π(i) = k_i / Σ_j k_j.
network-rule.emergent: Power-law degree distribution P(k) ~ k^-3; a few dominant hubs.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'attach_preferential' adds a node, samples m targets weighted by degree, writes edges.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 2 — the canonical growth rule; visibly grows hubs on screen.

network-rule.name: Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring
network-rule.summary: Interpolates regular lattice → random graph: start from a ring lattice and rewire each edge at random with probability p, yielding high clustering with short path lengths at intermediate p.
network-rule.rule: Begin with a k-regular ring lattice; for each edge, with probability p move one endpoint to a uniformly random node (no self/multi-edges).
network-rule.emergent: Small-world regime — high clustering, low diameter — for 0 < p << 1.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'rewire_edge' detaches one endpoint of an existing edge and reattaches at random w.p. p.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 3 — watch a tidy ring dissolve into a small world as p sweeps up.

network-rule.name: Bianconi–Barabási fitness ("fit-get-richer")
network-rule.summary: Preferential attachment weighted by an intrinsic per-node fitness, so a latecomer with high fitness can overtake older hubs — unlike pure BA.
network-rule.rule: New node attaches to i with probability Π(i) ∝ η_i · k_i, where η_i is a fitness drawn from a fixed distribution ρ(η).
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'attach_fitness' weights target sampling by η_i·k_i; η stored on node schema.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 4 — contrast with BA: show a young high-fitness node climbing to hub status.

network-rule.name: Duplication–divergence (biological growth)
network-rule.summary: Genome-evolution analogue: a new node copies an existing node's edges, then each copied edge is independently retained or dropped — reproduces observed protein-interaction network topology.
network-rule.rule: Pick a random node u; add a duplicate v inheriting all of u's edges; retain each inherited edge with probability q (optionally add a u–v link w.p. p).
network-rule.emergent: Power-law tail; non-self-averaging — identical params yield a wide family of networks.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'duplicate_divergent' copies a node's edge set then prunes each copied edge w.p. 1-q.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 5 — the biologically-motivated rule; bridges toward the SBML-at-nodes phase.

network-rule.name: Forest-fire growth (densification)
network-rule.summary: New nodes "burn" recursively outward from an anchor, linking to a random subset of neighbors at each hop — the first generator to reproduce graph densification and shrinking diameter over time.
network-rule.rule: New node picks an ambassador, links to it, then recursively links to a geometrically-distributed sample of the ambassador's out/in-neighbors.
network-rule.emergent: Densification power law (edges super-linear in nodes); diameter shrinks as the graph grows.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'forest_fire_attach' runs a bounded BFS burn from an anchor, writing edges to burned nodes.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 6 — the time-evolution rule; densification is striking in the animation.

network-rule.name: Adaptive / coevolutionary rewiring
network-rule.summary: Topology and node state coevolve: nodes rewire their links in response to the dynamics running on them (e.g. cut ties to "infected"/dissimilar neighbors, form ties to similar ones) — the natural bridge between Family A and Family B.
network-rule.rule: Per step, with rate w a node drops an edge to a neighbor in a disfavored state and reconnects to a random (or state-matched) node; node states update by an on-network process (SIS, voter, …).
network-rule.emergent: Self-organized topology, dynamic equilibria, bistability; small rule tweaks → drastic topology shifts.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'adaptive_rewire' reads neighbor state, conditionally detaches + reattaches; couples to a Family-B node process.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 7 — the coevolution capstone of Family A; explicitly links topology to on-node dynamics.

network-rule.name: Activity-driven temporal networks
network-rule.summary: Instead of a growing graph, a sequence of instantaneous contact graphs: each node fires with its own activity rate and, when active, connects to a few random others for one time window, then the edges vanish.
network-rule.rule: Each node i has activity a_i ∝ x_i (x_i ~ F(x)); per step i activates w.p. a_i·Δt and creates m edges to random nodes; all edges reset next step.
network-rule.emergent: Time-integrated degree reproduces the activity distribution; sets the stage for spreading on temporal graphs.
network-rule.pbg_reaction: reaction 'activity_fire' clears the edge set each step, then for each active node writes m random edges.
network-rule.role_in_investigation: Study 8 — temporal (blinking) networks; contrasts accreting vs. instantaneous topology.

network-dynamics.name: Epidemic spreading (SIS / SIR)
network-dynamics.summary: Canonical contagion: each node is Susceptible/Infected(/Recovered); infection transmits along edges, recovery is spontaneous — threshold behavior is set by network topology (vanishing threshold on scale-free hubs).
network-dynamics.rule: S→I at rate β per infected neighbor; I→S (SIS) or I→R (SIR) at rate μ.
network-dynamics.node_state: discrete (S/I/R) — the entry point before continuous SBML states.
network-dynamics.role_in_investigation: Study 9 — simplest dynamics ON a (fixed or rule-grown) network; discrete node state.

network-dynamics.name: Reaction–diffusion metapopulation (SBML-at-nodes template)
network-dynamics.summary: Each node is a well-mixed reactor holding continuous concentrations of multiple species that react locally; species diffuse/transport between connected nodes along edges. The template for the SBML-simulator-per-node phase.
network-dynamics.rule: Local: dX_i/dt = R(X_i) (node reaction network / SBML model). Coupling: diffusive flux D·(X_j − X_i) along each edge (i,j), optionally scaled by edge weight.
network-dynamics.node_state: continuous, multi-species (an SBML model instance per node).
network-dynamics.pbg_reaction: topology set by a Family-A rule; each node runs an SBML Process; a transport Process moves species across edges.
network-dynamics.role_in_investigation: Study 10+ — the headline later phase: continuous multi-species dynamics ON an evolving network with inter-node transport.

network-dynamics.name: Kuramoto synchronization
network-dynamics.summary: Each node is a phase oscillator with its own natural frequency, pulled toward its neighbors' phases; the network undergoes a transition to collective synchrony as coupling increases — topology shapes the transition.
network-dynamics.node_state: continuous scalar (phase) — a gentle continuous-dynamics example.
network-dynamics.role_in_investigation: Optional on-network study — a visually compelling continuous example (phases locking).

network-dynamics.name: Voter / consensus dynamics
network-dynamics.summary: Opinion dynamics: a random node copies the state of a random neighbor; network structure governs whether the system reaches consensus and how fast.
network-dynamics.rule: Pick node i and neighbor j at random; set state(i) ← state(j).
network-dynamics.role_in_investigation: Optional on-network study — pairs naturally with adaptive rewiring (Family A coevolution).
